rules.title: Ban on using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade (AB 325)
rules.requirement: Landlords, property managers and software vendors may not use or distribute a shared pricing algorithm (software that uses competitor data to recommend or set prices or terms) as part of an agreement or conspiracy to restrain trade. This applies to rent-setting software. Renters harmed may report it to the Attorney General or sue under the Cartwright Act.
rules.key_value: Unlawful to use/distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy in restraint of trade
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person (not the end consumer) who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm, meaning a method or software used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term. Applies to all products and services, including residential rents.
rules.exemptions: End consumers are not 'persons' under the section.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(a) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.penalty: Cartwright Act remedies; violation is punishable as a crime (per Legislative Counsel's Digest).

unresolvable_conditions: whether the landlord uses a common pricing algorithm that uses competitor data

rules.title: Ban on coercing adoption of prices recommended by a common pricing algorithm (AB 325)
rules.requirement: A person who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm may not pressure another person into setting or adopting the price or commercial term the algorithm recommends, such as forcing landlords to accept software-recommended rents.
rules.key_value: Unlawful to coerce adoption of algorithm-recommended price or commercial term
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person (not the end consumer) using or distributing a common pricing algorithm who coerces another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term (including level of service, availability, output) for the same or similar products or services in California.
rules.exemptions: End consumers are not 'persons' under the section.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729(b) (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.quoted_span: (b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
rules.penalty: Cartwright Act remedies; violation is punishable as a crime (per Legislative Counsel's Digest).

unresolvable_conditions: whether the landlord uses a common pricing algorithm and was coerced or coerces adoption of its recommendations

notes: AB 325 was chaptered Oct 6, 2025 (Ch. 338). The document gives no effective date. A regular California statute normally takes effect Jan 1, 2026, so the status is in_force, but effective_date is left null because the document doesn't support a date. The law is a general antitrust (Cartwright Act) measure, not specific to housing. It is classified as algorithmic_rent_setting because it covers rent-pricing software. Section 16756.1 (a looser pleading standard for Cartwright Act complaints) is procedural and is not recorded as its own rule. It does make algorithmic-collusion claims easier to bring.
